header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Morales (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Lena Cho (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (CobaltPay - Head of Infra); Priya Nair (CobaltPay - Security); Ethan Gomez (CobaltPay - ML Platform)
summary: Discovery focused on Private VPC deployment options, network connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region support, and security/compliance requirements. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; main blockers are CIDR overlap, cross-account peering policy, and KMS/HSM integration for key management.
topics: Intro/qualify current stack; Network topology and constraints; Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SAML); Region and data residency; PrivateLink vs VPC peering tradeoffs; Next steps/POC planning
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm jenna from Redwood Inference, our se Samir is here and Lena as well.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Hi, Marcus here. We're excited to understand the private deployment options, we run most of our infra in eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya here, i'll be looking at security and KMS / key mgmt requirements.
[00:36] Samir Patel: Great — quick agenda, want to cover current infra, network constraints, redwood private topologies (VPC peering, private endpoints), region support, and next steps.
[00:52] Ethan Gomez: To be upfront, our main ask is that data never traverses public internet and we need to integrate with our KMS and audit logs. Also low latency for token generation for our payment auth workflows.
[01:10] Jenna Morales: Understood. can you run through your current network setup? CIDRs, multiple accounts, transit gateway, that kind of thing.
[01:22] Marcus Lee: Sure. we have two AWS org accounts for prod and infra, prod VPC is 10.0.0.0/16 (eu-west-1) and 10.1.0.0/16 in us-east-1. we use a transit gateway for cross-AZ peering inside the org, and we currently do not allow third-party VPC peering inbound to prod without review.
[01:40] Priya Nair: We also have strict egress rules - no inbound public IPs to our subnets, and everything passes through our NAT and perimeter firewall.
[01:52] Samir Patel: OK that's helpful. there are two common patterns Redwood supports for Private: 1) VPC peering / TGW attachment to a Redwood-managed VPC 2) Private endpoints - we can provision interface endpoints (similar to AWS PrivateLink) into your VPC. each has tradeoffs.
[02:10] Jenna Morales: For Dedicated offering, it's a reserved pool of infra we operate; Private is where we place the inference control plane in a private network and either peer or expose private endpoints.
[02:24] Marcus Lee: Do you support cross-region private endpoints? we have some workloads in eu-west-1 but also us-east-1; ideal is to keep traffic in-region.
[02:34] Samir Patel: Short answer: we prefer deploying in-region where your VPC exists. PrivateLink is regional — cross-region PrivateLink isn't native, so we'd recommend deploying Redwood Private in the same region as your VPC or run a dedicated deployment in each region. there are options with transit gateway but that adds complexity and latency.
[02:54] Priya Nair: On KMS / HSM — can we bring our own keys (BYOK)? we need envelope encryption with our KMS and logs to our audit pipeline.
[03:06] Lena Cho: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; for BYOK we can integrate with your KMS or use an HSM-backed flow depending on compliance. audit logs and request-level logging can be forwarded to your SIEM, we have syslog/forwarding options and S3 delivery for audit artifacts.
[03:26] Ethan Gomez: Any constraints on subnet sizes or ENI limits? our infra team is worried about interface endpoint limits.
[03:34] Samir Patel: Good question. interface endpoints require ENIs per AZ; large fleets need larger subnets to avoid ENI exhaustion. with peering you avoid additional ENIs but peering has CIDR overlap constraints. we usually ask for at least /20 subnets for endpoints if you expect heavy concurrency.
[03:52] Marcus Lee: CIDR overlap is a sticking point — we can't change our CIDRs. Do you support AWS Transit Gateway attachment rather than direct peering?
[04:02] Samir Patel: Yes, TGW attachment is supported — Redwood can attach to your TGW. that helps avoid direct peering and simplifies multiple account topologies. but note we still need route table entries and a static route configuration; also TGW cross-region attaches can be more complex.
[04:22] Priya Nair: What's your plan for authentication and access control? we need SSO/SAML and RBAC, and least privilege for service accounts.
[04:34] Lena Cho: Redwood integrates with SAML SSO and supports role-based access controls. For API calls from your services to Redwood Private, you can use mTLS or private API keys stored in your secret manager; we also support OIDC in some flows. we'll include the exact auth flows in the security packet.
[04:54] Jenna Morales: Also to flag — we do per-route/model audit logs and token-level cost breakdowns in the console, which customers often push into their SIEM.
[05:06] Ethan Gomez: For latency targets, what SLOs does Redwood provide on Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:14] Samir Patel: Hosted is lowest friction, but depending on region it may add egress hops. Dedicated gives predictable throughput on reserved GPU pools; Private is focused on isolation and minimizing public network hops. Latency depends on deployment region and your proximity to the cluster; typical 99p token latency numbers we share in the performance sheet — we'll include those benchmarks.
[05:36] Marcus Lee: Are there any restrictions around IP allowlists? we have strict egress filtering — we prefer pushing a small set of IPs or using private endpoints.
[05:46] Lena Cho: With Private endpoints you won't need public IPs. For peering / TGW you'll add routes and security groups; we can provide the minimal set of ports (TLS 443, some health-check ports) and CIDR pairs to allow.
[06:00] Priya Nair: Does Redwood require supplier-side VPC in our account or do you host endpoints in your own account and peer?
[06:10] Samir Patel: We can do both. Option A: Redwood provisions an account-managed VPC and peers to yours (we request a peering or TGW attach). Option B: We provision interface endpoints inside your account via PrivateLink provisioning — this is usually preferred for strict security teams because the network resides in your account. Both have pros/cons on operational burden.
[06:34] Marcus Lee: For option B — who manages the lifecycle of those ENIs and endpoints? we don't want a lot of manual ops.
[06:42] Jenna Morales: Redwood automates endpoint lifecycle via terraform / IaC patterns we provide; Samir, we can show a sample module.
[06:50] Samir Patel: yes, we have terraform modules and example CloudFormation; we can automate creation and rotation of endpoints and certificates. we'll share code snippets.
[07:04] Ethan Gomez: Any PCI considerations? we handle payments; does private deployment help with PCI compliance?
[07:12] Priya Nair: PCI is mostly about data handling and segmentation — keeping inference in a private VPC and integrating with our KMS helps. need to confirm that Redwood's processing won't persist cardholder data unless we opt-in; that's a policy conversation.
[07:26] Lena Cho: We can control data retention policies and model usage. by default we do not retain customer input beyond necessary logs unless configured otherwise; again we'll include retention options in the security packet.
[07:40] Marcus Lee: Logging — can we centralize logs to our S3 bucket?
[07:44] Samir Patel: Yes, we support S3 delivery for audit logs and also streaming to your SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose.
[07:52] Jenna Morales: Quick demo note: for the POC we'd propose a small smoke test in eu-west-1 using PrivateLink — spin up a small cluster, validate KMS integration and perf for your auth path.
[08:06] Marcus Lee: That sounds good. timeline wise we want to run a POC in August and decide by mid-September.
[08:14] Priya Nair: We'll need security review materials before committing to a POC.
[08:20] Jenna Morales: Absolutely — i'll send SOC2 report, KMS docs, network runbook, and terraform examples.
[08:28] Ethan Gomez: About regions — you mentioned some customers have needed multi-region deployments. if we need eu-west-1 and us-east-1, do we need two Private clusters?
[08:38] Samir Patel: Generally yes for strict in-region requirements — one cluster per region to avoid cross-region traffic. We can discuss multi-region replication patterns but typically separate deploys are simplest.
[08:52] Marcus Lee: One more: what's the maintenance window and how do you handle upgrades on Private? we need to schedule around our peak times.
[09:02] Lena Cho: Maintenance windows are configurable. for Private deployments we coordinate upgrades with your infra team; we support canary and rollback policies and can do rolling restarts to minimize impact.
[09:18] Priya Nair: Are there any gotchas with MTU or fragmentation when crossing TGW? last time we had issues with jumbo frames.
[09:26] Samir Patel: It's mostly standard network troubleshooting — we'll document recommended MTU and packet size settings. We also recommend end-to-end testing with iperf in the POC.
[09:36] Marcus Lee: On costs — how different is Private vs Dedicated? at a high-level.
[09:42] Jenna Morales: Dedicated is often more cost-efficient at high sustained throughput because it's reserved GPU pools. Private adds networking and possibly per-region infra costs. We'll provide a TCO comparison in the follow-up.
[09:54] Ethan Gomez: For the POC, could you give a rough set of perf numbers for our auth path (low context length, 128 tokens) so we can compare?
[10:04] Samir Patel: We'll pull numbers from similar customers and include them; expect single-digit millisecond token latencies for small contexts in-region on Private/Dedicated, but we'll verify with a targeted benchmark.
[10:18] Priya Nair: Ok, sounds like we have enough to start internal sign-off.
[10:22] Jenna Morales: Great. recap of next steps: i'll share security packet and terraform snippets; Marcus will send CIDRs and network contact; Samir will set up the tech deep dive. any other questions?
[10:36] Marcus Lee: None from me. thanks.
[10:40] Ethan Gomez: Thanks all.
[10:44] Jenna Morales: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[10:50] [meeting ends]

Note: transcription contains typical auto-transcription artifacts (word swaps, run-on lines). Some proper nouns may be mis-heard in places.
